s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual disturbance in a patient with a history of breast cancer and recent initiation of hormonal therapy
salient_findings: Parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes
key_facts: 69-year-old woman
History of hypertension
History of stage IA estrogen receptor–positive and progesterone receptor–positive and ERBB/neu receptor–negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast
Started receiving 1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to presentation
Not using any other notable medications
Denied any recent changes to her regimen
Never previously used tamoxifen
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/40 OD and 20/25 OS
Pupils were equal, round, and reactive without an afferent pupillary defect
Intraocular pressures were normal
Anterior segment examination was notable for mild cataracts in both eyes
Fundus examination was notable for parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes

shortlist.label: Tamoxifen retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of breast cancer and is on hormonal therapy, which is a known risk factor for tamoxifen retinopathy, although the patient is on anastrozole, the clinical presentation is similar

shortlist.label: Anastrozole retinal toxicity
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is on anastrozole, which is a known risk factor for retinal toxicity, and the clinical presentation matches the known side effects of the medication

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes is consistent with Bietti crystalline retinopathy

shortlist.label: Crystalline retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of crystalline deposits in the retina is consistent with crystalline retinopathy, although this is a broader category that includes Bietti crystalline retinopathy

shortlist.label: Canthaxanthin retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of crystalline deposits in the retina is also consistent with canthaxanthin retinopathy, although this is less likely given the patient's medication history

raw.rationale: The patient started receiving 1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to presentation and presented with parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes, which is consistent with anastrozole retinal toxicity.

rejected.label: Tamoxifen retinopathy
rejected.why: The patient had never previously used tamoxifen.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline retinopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic or other ocular findings typical of Bietti crystalline retinopathy.

rejected.label: Crystalline retinopathy
rejected.why: This is a more general term and does not specify the cause of the crystalline deposits.

rejected.label: Canthaxanthin retinopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of the patient using canthaxanthin, a carotenoid that can cause crystalline retinopathy.
